newsitem.title: USA: UPS says 15,000 Teamsters jobs at risk after strike.
newsitem.headline: UPS says 15,000 Teamsters jobs at risk after strike.

text.p: United Parcel Service said on Tuesday that nearly 15,000 Teamsters jobs were at risk and 5 percent of its business could be lost as a result of the 15-day strike against the company.

"As we finished the first two weeks of the strike we had determined that the amount of volume that was at risk of permanent loss would result in a possible 15,000 jobs," UPS spokesman Ken Sternad told CNN. "Those 15,000 were Teamsters jobs."

Those jobs at risk of loss may be "the people who pick up and sort and deliver the packages, and we can equate very easily that when we lose packages how many Teamsters jobs that will be," Sternad said.
"Hopefully through growth they will come back but we've lost business over the past two weeks."
When asked by CNN how much business the company may have lost, he said: "It could be somewhere in the neighborhood of 5 percent that it's as risk of losing."
